topic: What if you could teleport anywhere you've seen?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
TELEPORT ANYWHERE?

power.rule: teleport anywhere you have seen with your own eyes
power.look: cyan flash ring, camera jitter, cyan eye glint

script.text: Locked out? Blink. In your room.
Late for class? Blink. In your seat.
Rooftop sunset? Blink. On the edge.
What if you could teleport anywhere you've seen?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: Earth rotates at a thousand miles an hour. Teleport between latitudes, and you hit the ground at five hundred miles an hour. That's real.
So which way are you facing?

science.claim: Earth rotates at a thousand miles an hour, and teleporting between latitudes slams you into the ground at five hundred miles an hour.
science.working: Linear velocity from Earth's rotation is v = omega * R * cos(latitude). At the equator (lat 0), v = 1,040 mph (465 m/s). At latitude 60 degrees north, cos(60) = 0.5, so v = 520 mph (232 m/s). Conservation of momentum dictates the teleported body retains its original tangential velocity, producing a horizontal velocity delta relative to the new ground of over 500 mph (232 m/s).
science.source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet; Conservation of Linear Momentum
